lessons.title: Find your one reader
lessons.hook: Write for one reader, and the rest follow.
lessons.chart: Open rate by audience focus, last 10 weeks
lessons.summary: Pick the one person each issue is for, and let every choice follow from them: the subject line, the length, the send time.

lessons.title: Write a sign-up page that converts
lessons.hook: A promise, a proof, a single field.
lessons.summary: Rebuild your sign-up page around one promise, one piece of proof and one field, then measure it for a week.

lessons.title: Your first 100 subscribers
lessons.hook: The first hundred come by hand.
lessons.chart: New subscribers per week, first 10 weeks
lessons.summary: Ask people you know, one at a time, and turn each yes into two more introductions.

lessons.title: Turn readers into referrers
lessons.hook: Every reader can bring the next one.
lessons.summary: Referral programs work when the reward feels earned and the ask feels natural. In this lesson you set up a three-step referral ladder, write the one-line ask that closes every issue, and see how The Margin Notes now gets 21% of its signups from readers sharing it.
lessons.more: We also cover where the referral link should sit, how to choose rewards that cost nothing to deliver, and the two numbers to watch in Analytics each week: share rate and referral conversion.
takeaways: Ask once per issue, right after your most useful paragraph.
Reward milestones at 1, 3 and 10 referrals, digital rewards first.
Check share rate weekly and aim for 2% of opens.

transcript.text: Most of your next readers already know one of your current ones.
The ask: one line, at the end of your most useful paragraph, every issue.
The ladder: a thank-you at one referral, a bonus issue at three, a call at ten.
In Analytics, watch share rate and referral conversion; ignore the rest for now.
Your homework: write the ask, set the first rung, and send it Thursday.

lessons.title: Grow with cross-promotions
lessons.hook: Borrow an audience, lend yours back.
lessons.summary: Find three newsletters your readers also read, and trade a recommendation that sounds like you.

lessons.title: Keep out of the promotions tab
lessons.hook: Land in the inbox, not the tab.
lessons.summary: Fewer links, plainer text, a reply from new readers: the habits that keep each issue in the primary inbox.

lessons.title: Launch a paid tier
lessons.hook: Charge for the part they'd miss.
lessons.summary: Decide what stays free, what is worth paying for, and the one price to start with.

lessons.title: Measure what matters
lessons.summary: Set up a Monday review of growth, engagement and revenue, and drop every figure that doesn't change a decision.

guides.title: Write subject lines people open
guides.summary: Curiosity, a number, and the reader's own words: three patterns that lift opens without tricks.
steps: Write five subject lines for every issue, then pick by reading them aloud.
Lead with the reader's problem, not your topic.
Test one change at a time on a tenth of the list.

guides.title: Grow with a referral program
guides.summary: A referral ladder readers want to climb, and the one-line ask that keeps it moving.
steps: Put the referral link right after your most useful paragraph.
Reward the first referral at once, with something digital.
Show each reader how close they are to the next reward.

guides.title: Price your paid tier
guides.summary: Find the part of your newsletter readers would miss, and the price that matches it.
steps: List what readers reply about most: that is what they value.
Start with one monthly and one yearly price, two months free.
Raise prices for new readers only, and say so.

guides.title: Fix spam-folder placement
guides.summary: SPF, DKIM, list hygiene and inbox placement checks.
steps: Check SPF, DKIM and DMARC on your sending domain.
Remove readers who haven't opened in 90 days, after one last note.
Send a test to a seed list before every issue.

guides.title: Build a welcome series
guides.summary: Three emails that turn a new subscriber into a reader who expects you.
steps: Send the first email at once, with your best issue.
Ask a question in the second, and answer every reply.
Point to the archive and the referral program in the third.

guides.title: Sell sponsorships that renew
guides.summary: Price by the readers who click, report like a partner, and get the second booking before the first runs.
steps: Price per thousand engaged readers, not per thousand sent.
Send every sponsor a one-page report within a week.
Offer the renewal with the report.

guides.title: Warm up a new sending domain
guides.summary: Ramp volume slowly so a new domain stays out of spam.
steps: Start with your most engaged readers.
Double the volume every few sends while bounces stay low.
Watch complaints more than opens.

guides.title: Find a voice readers come back for
guides.summary: Write the way you talk to one friend, and keep the habits that make you recognisable.
steps: Read your last issue aloud and cut what you wouldn't say.
Keep a list of phrases you overuse.
Open with a scene, not a summary.

guides.title: Turn social posts into signups
guides.summary: Share one useful idea from each issue, with a link that promises the rest.
steps: Pull one idea per issue into a post that stands alone.
End with what the newsletter adds, not a plain link.
Track which posts bring readers who stay.
